**NTRT Pre-Market Gap Brief — 2026-10-28 (Wed)**

- **Mode B — screener fallback.** The `ntrt_mtrt` backend was unreachable from this runtime (`GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/health` → connection refused, no `NTRT_BASE_URL` set), and the spec's `mcp__tradingview__screen_stocks` is not registered here.
- The market-wide pre-market screen was therefore run off the **Yahoo predefined screener** (universe + `preMarketChangePercent`) with every headline print confirmed on the **Nasdaq public pre-market tape**, and catalysts from press.
- No figure in this brief comes from a source that did not return 200 with a parseable body.

**Snapshot window:** 09:00–09:10 ET. Prints younger than 10 minutes old at capture time.

- **Caveat that changes how to read this:** the pre-market is thin.
- Of 1,246 screened symbols, 908 printed pre-market and 86 of those are ≥$200M market cap with a ≥3% gap —
- but a large share of those 86 traded fewer than 50,000 shares. A gap with 2,000 shares of volume is a quote, not a market.
- The "importance" column below is the filter, and names whose gap rests on under ~1% of a normal day's volume are marked **thin**.

**TL;DR**

- **Two clean, opposite theses are colliding in the tape.** AI data-center capex winners ripped:
- VRT +15.4% on a 61% revenue beat and a raised year, FLEX +12.9% on record EPS and a 9% guidance hike, UCTT +13.3% on a record quarter, with APH +6.8%, NVT +6.3%, MOD +7.0% and EXTR +7.8% as read-through.
- Residential-solar and guidance-cut complex ripped the other way: ENPH -20.3% on a double miss plus a Q4 guide 20% below consensus, dragging SEDG -9.6% and RUN -4.8% with it.
- **The two biggest single-name events are idiosyncratic, not thematic.** WEN +15.7% on a $1.4B/$7.35-per-share take-private offer from Trian's Peltz consortium, and ULBI +144.8% on EnerSys buying the battery maker for $16 a share in cash.
- Both are single-print specials, not sector signals.
- **Guidance is the dividing line, not the beats.** VRT, FLEX, UCTT, GEHC and PPG all *beat and raised*.
- BSX (-11.3%) and NXPI (-7.9%) both *beat and cut*, and were sold hard —
- BSX on a cyberattack-driven FY26 guidance trim, NXPI on a Q4 operating-margin guide that came in under the Street even with a 19% revenue growth quarter.

**Catalysts — the five deep dives**

Deep dives were capped at five per the spec; everything else above is a one-line press attribution from the same morning's coverage.

- **ENPH (-20.3%) —
- a double miss and a guide 20% under consensus.** Q3 adjusted EPS of $0.41 against a $0.51 consensus and revenue of $293.3M against $303.9M ($410.4M a year ago).
- The Q4 revenue guide of $225–255M (midpoint $240M) is the bigger problem: consensus was ~$300.5M, so the company is guiding to a *second* sequential decline.
- CEO Badri Kothandaraman pointed at higher rates and the expiry of the Section 25D federal tax credit for US residential solar, plus an ~11% sequential European revenue drop (France weakest).
- JPMorgan cut its target to $29 from $35; GLJ holds a Sell. The stock is pressing toward its 52-week low of $25.77. Solar peer SEDG went with it on read-through.
- **INTA (-16.2%) — a revenue miss that swallowed an EPS beat.** Fiscal Q1 non-GAAP EPS of $0.44 was fine;
- revenue of $125.5M against ~$159.2M expected was not, and the shortfall is attributed to the on-premises-to-cloud subscription transition, which pushes bookings between periods.
- Q2 guidance came in below estimates and Raymond James reiterated Market Perform on "mixed dynamics around bookings timing" while noting record 75.82% gross margin.
- This is the largest single-name drop of the day with a *thin* pre-market tape (13,154 shares) — treat the -16% as a headline, not a price.
- **VRT (+15.4%) — the cleanest beat-and-raise of the morning, and the read-through engine.** Q3 net sales $4.313B, +61% y/y against a $3.75–3.76B consensus; adjusted EPS $2.21 vs $1.82, +78%;
- adjusted operating margin 25.2% (+290bp). Organic orders more than doubled y/y, which directly addresses the AI-project-delay worry.
- FY26 sales guidance went to $14.45–14.85B (mid $14.65B, up $650M from July) and adjusted EPS to $7.10–7.20 (mid $7.15 vs $6.73 consensus); Q4 guide $4.41B / $2.25 also above.
- CEO Giordano Albertazzi: "we are in the middle of the largest infrastructure buildout and it's accelerating." The tape extends this across the power-and-thermal chain — APH, NVT, MOD, EXTR —
- and it is the single most consequential theme in today's tape.
- **UCTT (+13.3%) —
- record results, and a WFE callout.** Adjusted EPS $1.15 vs $0.94 consensus, revenue $759M (+49% y/y) vs $728M, non-GAAP gross margin 17.3% (from 15.7%) and operating margin 9.0% (from 7.0%).
- Q4 guide $800–860M (mid $830M) sat slightly above the $813.9M consensus with EPS of $1.11–1.35.
- The forward-looking kicker was the CEO's expectation that 2027 wafer-fab equipment spend could exceed **$200B**, supporting cleanroom expansion in Malaysia, Cebu, Singapore and Czechia. Needham kept Buy.
- Note the price history: 52-week high $144.22, low $21.48.
- **FLEX (+12.9%) —
- a beat with a guidance raise, and a live catalyst underneath.** FQ2 net sales $8.49B (+25% y/y) vs $8.15B consensus, record adjusted EPS $1.18 vs $1.06, adjusted operating margin 7.1% (from 6.0%), $501M operating cash flow.
- FY27 revenue guide raised to $34.9–35.9B (mid $35.4B vs $35.1B consensus) and adjusted EPS to $4.84–5.16 (mid $5.00 vs $4.62). The Q3 guide of $9.02B implies +28% growth.
- Management is also advancing the planned **spin-off of the Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment**, which is part of why the data-center complex bid this name.
- BofA had already flagged the setup with a Buy and a $150 target cut from $180.

**Themes**

- **AI data-center capex is the dominant bid.** VRT, FLEX, UCTT, APH, NVT, MOD, EXTR, TER, EVR and LFUS are all electrical/thermal/networking names and the group is bid almost regardless of whether the individual print was confirmed.
- The one thing to keep straight is that the tape is pricing a *capex supercycle*, not a general risk-on move —
- the S&P 500 was only +0.1% and the Nasdaq +0.4–0.6% in pre-market indications, so the dispersion is company-specific earnings, not index beta.

- **Residential solar is the mirror image.** ENPH's guide was a demand-and-policy problem, and it took SEDG (-9.6%), RUN (-4.8%) and the broader resi-solar complex with it.
- ENPH's own IQ Solid-State Transformer AI/data-center pipeline (50+ potential customers, including a major cloud provider) is the irony of the day:
- the growth story is data center, the guidance is residential.

- **Guidance beats headlines.** Every name that sold off hard today beat the quarter and cut the guide (BSX, NXPI, INTA) or missed revenue outright (INTA, WING).
- Every large name that ripped beat *and* raised (VRT, FLEX, UCTT, GEHC, PPG). The market is trading the second line of guidance, not the print.

- **Event-driven names are in the book, not the theme.** WEN (take-private), ULBI (acquired for $16 cash), GEV (Trench Group, ~$9B) and ENS (the acquirer) are single-print specials that happen to sit in the same tape.

**Needs human eyes**

- **WEN is nearly at the deal price.** At $7.10–7.11 pre-market against a $7.35 cash offer, ~97% of the spread is already captured.
- The residual upside is the confirmation risk on a non-binding proposal; the downside if Trian walks is a fast round-trip to the $6.14 close.
- This is a spread trade, not a gap trade.
- **ULBI's market cap is below the screen's floor.** TradingView puts Ultralife at ~$106M (CNBC's deal value implies ~$320M).
- It is the largest mover of the day by a factor of seven and it is sub-scale — it would have been invisible to a $200M filter.
- Anyone using this screen with a hard market-cap floor is blind to it.
- **Two prints disagree with themselves.** RGC's composite shows +7.24% at $8.00 while the last trade is $7.63 at 08:55 ET, and ULCC's composite (+7.60% at $5.95) sits below its 09:09 last trade of $6.14.
- Both need a live quote before anyone sizes them.
- **Thin-tape gaps.** INTA (-16.2% on 13,154 shares), CSGP (-6.8% on 28,917), UHS (-5.7% on 2,599), MIR (-7.3% on 14,665), EXTR (+7.8% on 6,991), EVR (+7.8% on 1,772) and NVT (+6.3% on 9,617) each traded well under 1% of a normal day's volume.
- The percentage is real; the size behind it is not.
- **Two macro events land today.** The **FOMC decision at 2:00 PM ET** is the day's dominant macro risk —
- a late-session reversal in the data-center complex is a live possibility, and FOMC also explains the muted index bid.
- **Ford reports after the close**, which matters for STLA's +8.7% and the auto complex.
- **SKHY is an ADR, not a US listing** — +6.9% on record Q3 AI-memory results and a special dividend tied to the Kioxia stake.
- Sizing it in the US session carries overnight Korea gap risk in both directions.
- **A gap can fade before 09:30.** Pre-market volume is a running counter and several names sit near their high/low of the session range. Nothing here is a 09:30 open instruction.

**Method & data caveats**

- The universe came from Yahoo's predefined screener across seven lists (day_gainers, day_losers, most_actives, small_cap_gainers, most_shorted_stocks, undervalued_growth_stocks, growth_technology_stocks):
- **1,246 unique symbols, 908 with a pre-market print, 516 with a print ≤30 minutes old.** Ranked on `preMarketChangePercent` —
- *not* on the prior session's move, because the session-based lists would have hidden the day's best pre-market movers.
- Names that gapped on news without a prior-session move (ULBI, LOGI) are absent from the screener universe and were added from press coverage, then verified on the tape.
- The 10% floor on market cap used the TradingView `market_cap_basic` field, which for US listings is in USD.
- 86 names qualified at ≥$200M and a ≥3% gap (57 up, 29 down).
- **TradingView's `relative_volume_10d_calc` is a daily proxy, not intraday relative volume**, and it runs systematically ~5–20% below a true trailing 10-session average, so it flatters high-RVOL names.
- The "PM vol (% of 3M ADV)" column is the more honest importance measure and is computed from Yahoo's `averageDailyVolume3Month` against the Nasdaq pre-market volume counter.
- **The TradingView `america` scanner has no pre-market columns** — `premarket_price`, `premarket_change_percent` and `premarket_volume` all returned null across the universe.
- It was used for sector, industry, market cap and relative volume only.
- Pre-market percentages are taken from the Nasdaq `extended-trading` composite string;
- where the composite and the last trade disagree by more than ~1.5pp (VRT, BSX, TER, IP, LOGI), the last trade is shown separately in the table's "PM last" column so the reader can see the spread.
- Yahoo's `chart`, `spark` and custom screener POST endpoints were not used: this runtime is rate-limited on them (HTTP 429).
- The **predefined** screener endpoint answered 200 without a cookie or crumb and carries the live pre-market fields, which is what made a market-wide screen possible at all.
- Catalyst language is taken from morning press (Reuters, Barron's, Seeking Alpha, Investing.com, CNBC, Benzinga, company releases) and cross-checked against at least two independent outlets for each of the five deep dives.
- Where no catalyst could be confirmed, the row says so rather than guessing.
- No trading advice is given or implied. Nothing here is an instruction to transact.
